name: Dradie Ellen Kulp
notable_stories: She and her father, John Kulp, compiled extensive family information in silver ink on black-paged scrapbooks around 1943
Eloped with Ray Simons at age 17 after he stole her away to Ritzville
She compiled the Silver Ink family scrapbooks in 1943
Dradie, with her father John Kulp, made family scrapbooks for several siblings with black photo pages and family information in silver ink; her records stop about 1943.
A few years after Ray's death Dradie was in a nursing home in Pasco battling cancer; John and a cousin took her out to breakfast and had a lovely morning.
milestones: Raised six children on a Lynden dairy farm
sources: Family research emails, 2011–2013 (John and Barbara Adams with Irma Kulp Zacher, George F. Adams, Bill Allen and others)
John Howard Adams, "John Howard Adams - A Memoir" (privately printed)
notes: Siblings listed: Edith Sarah, Marlan John, Nardin Ira, Reta May, Elmer Spencer, Dorothy Belle, Ruth Zenith, Alton Roger, Audrey Rebecca
CORRECTION 2026-09-22: Mother set to mcphail_mary_emily, the only recorded wife of John Jacob Kulp (m. 15 Aug 1897; she d. 1931); confirmed by Brendan Adams.
Dradie was named in a line of several Dradie/Drady/Draden relatives, including her mother's sister Draden McPhail Dunbar. [Family research emails, email 49]

Unconfirmed: Family members disagree whether the first seven Kulp children were born at Delta Township, Blaine or Lynden; Irma believed they were born on the Kulp homestead on Burk Road. [Family research emails, email 48]
Open question: How far did Dradie, Edith, Marlan, Dorothy and Ruth Kulp get in school? Irma asks John to share anything he knows [Family research emails, email 48]
